d201.text: Last time, we opened four crates: plants, animals, fungi and bacteria. Now we are back in our community garden, with the plants crate.

d301.text: Lock in first. And find the new lizard!

d401.text: Plants can be classified into two groups: flowering plants and non-flowering plants.

d402.text: This chilli plant has no flowers today. So it is a non-flowering plant!

d403.text: Round one. Is Momo right? No flowers today. Only green chillies, with seeds inside. One, it is a flowering plant. Two, it is a non-flowering plant. Show me with your fingers.

d405.text: One! One is my lucky number.

d406.text: One. A chilli is a fruit. And fruits come from flowers.

d407.text: Watch this chilli plant. Speeded up.

d408.text: A small white flower. The petals drop. A tiny green chilli grows where the flower was.

d409.text: The answer is one. The flower developed into a fruit. And inside the fruit: seeds.

d411.text: A lucky number is not a reason, Basil. No point!

d502.text: Flowering plants bear flowers. They reproduce from seeds. The flowers in flowering plants develop into fruits. The seeds are found in the fruits.

d601.text: And this one? No flowers. No fruits.

d602.text: That is a bird's nest fern, Momo. It never has flowers. So how does it make new plants? Look under a leaf. Shrink down. Quietly.

d603.text: You are tiny now. You are under a fern leaf.

d604.text: Above you: brown spore bags, in neat rows.

d606.text: Out come the spores. As fine as dust. And you are one of them.

d609.text: In time, a new fern grows here.

d701.text: No flowers. No seeds. A fern reproduces from spores, kept in spore bags.

d703.text: Non-flowering plants do not bear flowers. They reproduce from spores that may be found in spore bags.

d704.text: Spores? Mushrooms have spores too! So a fern is a fungus?

d705.text: Good thinking, Basil. But a fern makes its own food when there is light. So it is a plant.

d802.text: One. Hibiscus: a flowering plant. Two. Bird's nest fern: a non-flowering plant. Three. Grass: a non-flowering plant.

d803.text: Showdown! Double points. One line has a mistake. Line one, two, or three? Show me with your fingers.

d805.text: Three! I hide in long grass. It has tiny flowers on top.

d808.text: Grass is a flowering plant. Its flowers are tiny. The grass-cutter usually cuts them off before we see them.

d810.text: Showed three fingers? Put up two more on your score hand!

d901.text: Plants are one of the four main groups. Remember all four?

ch01.text: Plants! Animals! Fungi! Bacteria! Four main groups of living things!

d1001.text: Show me your score hand! More than two? You beat the Buddies. Three fingers? High five!

d1002.text: Did you spot the lizard? It was on the tree trunk, under the fern. Does a new lizard come from a seed, a spore, or an egg? Tell someone at home.

d1101.text: Your turn. Find one flowering plant and one non-flowering plant near your home. Look. Do not pick.

d1102.text: Next time: animals! A frog. A bird. A fish. Feathers, scales, or moist skin? Lock in your answer for next time.

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?
